links.outcome: Compared simple ML model versus transformer models on the same data for predicting lifesaving intervention
links.effect: AUROC .793 for MLM vs .803 for BioBERT and DistilBERT; AP .670 vs .674 and .673. Performance was equivalent, and the LLMs needed far more computation, so the simpler model was sufficient.
links.quote: MLMs and LLMs produced broadly equivalent performance in predicting LSI (MLM: AUROC = .793 [.776, .810]; AP = .670 [.643, .695] vs. BioBERT: AUROC = .803 [.796, .816]; AP = .674 [.649, .698]) vs. DistilBERT: AUROC = .803 [.785, .811]; AP = .673 [.651, .688]).

links.outcome: Whether complex transformer models outperform simpler models and at what computational cost
links.effect: Transformers gave no meaningful performance gain (AUROC .803 vs .793). Training took 7:14 (BioBERT) and 3:57 (DistilBERT) vs 9.42 s for MLM. Prediction took 13.36 s and 7.37 s vs .048 s.
links.quote: Our findings counter the "bigger is better" paradigm in medical AI: MLMs performed equivalently to LLMs in task mirroring on-scene triage while requiring a fraction of the computational resources.

unlisted_practices: Prioritizing computational efficiency and edge-deployable, explainable models for military or resource-constrained settings

screen.reason: Retrospective benchmark comparing simpler ML ensemble models against smaller LLM/transformer models (DistilBERT/BioBERT) for computational efficiency and discrimination in prehospital triage.
